description: A single-panel table rendered as an image (Table 1), with no axes, curves, micrographs, colour scales or scale bars. The table is a one-row composition table whose header row prints the six element symbols C, Al, Mn, P, S and Fe left to right in a serif font, separated from the single data row by a horizontal rule. The data row gives the analysed chemical composition: C 0.29, Al 4.6, Mn 8.9, P < 0.005, S < 0.005 and Fe Balance. Every entry is printed as a plain number or inequality string; no uncertainties, repeat analyses, heat numbers or processing/annealing conditions appear anywhere in the table. The table carries the compositional basis for the whole study: the measured 8.9 Mn, 4.6 Al and 0.29 C correspond to the alloy designated Fe–9Mn–5Al-0.3C in the citing text, and the very low P and S entries indicate impurity-controlled melting consistent with the cited vacuum-induction 5 kg ingot. Nothing in the pixels contradicts the caption; the caption supplies the unit (wt. %), which is not printed inside the image itself.

observations.observation: The image is a two-row table: a header row of six element symbols (C, Al, Mn, P, S, Fe) and one data row, separated by a horizontal rule.
The data row prints P < 0.005 and S < 0.005, i.e. both are given as upper bounds rather than measured values.
The data row prints Fe as 'Balance'; the sum of the listed elements therefore completes to 100 %.
No unit, processing condition, heat number or uncertainty is printed inside the table image; only the caption states the compositions are in wt. %.
The citing text identifies the experimental steel as Fe-9Mn-5Al-0.3C, prepared in a 5 kg ingot by a vacuum induction furnace.

The citing text reports the steel density as 7.34 g*cm^-3 measured by the drainage method using Archimedes' principle, 6.7 % lower than that of low-carbon low-alloyed steels; this value is not shown in the table.
The measured compositions (8.9 Mn, 4.6 Al, 0.29 C) match the alloy designation 'Fe-9Mn-5Al-0.3C' used in the text as rounded nominal values.
